metadata.title: Clique Decompositions in Random Graphs via Refined Absorption

nodes.name: Yuster Conjecture for $G(n,p)$
nodes.statement: If $p \geq (1 + \varepsilon)\sqrt{(\log n)/n}$, then asymptotically almost surely $G(n,p)$ has a $K_3$-packing containing all but at most $3n$ edges.
conclusions: a.a.s. $G(n,p)$ has a $K_3$-packing with leave at most $3n$

nodes.name: Yuster Conjecture for $G_{n,d}$
nodes.statement: If $d \gg \sqrt{n \log n}$ and $d$ is even, then asymptotically almost surely $G_{n,d}$ has a $K_3$-decomposition provided $3 \mid d \cdot n$.
conclusions: a.a.s. $G_{n,d}$ has a $K_3$-decomposition

nodes.name: Yuster Triangle Packing in $G(n,p)$
nodes.statement: If $p \ge n^{-\frac{1}{3}+\beta}$ for some $\beta > 0$, then a.a.s. $G(n,p)$ has a $K_3$-packing containing all but at most $n+O(1)$ edges.
conclusions: a.a.s. $G(n,p)$ has a $K_3$-packing with leave $\le n + O(1)$

nodes.name: Yuster Triangle Decomposition for Random Regular
nodes.statement: If $d \ge n^{\frac{2}{3}+\beta}$ for some $\beta > 0$, $d$ is even, and $3 \mid d \cdot n$, then a.a.s. $G_{n,d}$ has a $K_3$-decomposition.
conclusions: a.a.s. $G_{n,d}$ has a $K_3$-decomposition

nodes.name: Yuster $K_q$-Packing in $G(n,p)$
nodes.statement: Let $q \ge 4$. If $p \ge n^{-\frac{1}{q+0.5}+\beta}$ for some $\beta > 0$, then a.a.s. $G(n,p)$ has a $K_q$-packing containing all but at most $(q-2)n+O(1)$ edges.
conclusions: a.a.s. $G(n,p)$ has a $K_q$-packing with leave $\le (q-2)n + O(1)$

nodes.name: Yuster $K_q$-Decomposition for Random Regular
nodes.statement: Let $q \ge 4$. If $d \ge n^{1-\frac{1}{q+0.5}+\beta}$, $(q-1)\mid d$, and $q \mid d\cdot n$, then a.a.s. $G_{n,d}$ has a $K_q$-decomposition.
conclusions: a.a.s. $G_{n,d}$ has a $K_q$-decomposition

nodes.name: $K_q$-Absorber
nodes.statement: Let $L$ be a $K_q$-divisible hypergraph. A hypergraph $A$ is a $K_q$-absorber for $L$ if $V(L) \subseteq V(A)$ is independent in $A$ and both $A$ and $L \cup A$ admit $K_q$-decompositions.

nodes.name: Maximum Rooted Density
nodes.statement: For a graph $H$ and an independent set $R \subseteq V(H)$, $m(H,R) := \max\{ e(H')/|V(H')\setminus R| : H' \subseteq H,\, V(H')\setminus R \ne \emptyset \}$.

nodes.name: Absorber Rooted $2$-Density Threshold $d_{\rm abs}(K_q)$
nodes.statement: The infimum over $r > 0$ such that for all $C_1$, there exists $C_2$ such that every $K_q$-divisible $L$ on at most $C_1$ vertices has a $K_q$-absorber $A$ on at most $C_2$ vertices with $m_2(A,V(L)) \le r$.

nodes.name: Yuster Random General
nodes.statement: Let $q\ge 3$ and $a := \max\{d_{\rm abs}(K_q),\, (q+1)/2\}$. If $p \ge n^{-1/a+\beta}$ for some $\beta > 0$, then a.a.s. $G(n,p)$ has a $K_q$-packing with leave at most $(q-2)n + O(1)$ edges.
conclusions: a.a.s. $G(n,p)$ has a $K_q$-packing with leave $\le (q-2)n + O(1)$

nodes.name: Yuster Random Regular General
nodes.statement: Let $q\ge 3$ and $a := \max\{d_{\rm abs}(K_q),\, (q+1)/2\}$. If $d \ge n^{1-1/a+\beta}$, $(q-1)\mid d$, and $q\mid d\cdot n$, then a.a.s. $G_{n,d}$ has a $K_q$-decomposition.
conclusions: a.a.s. $G_{n,d}$ has a $K_q$-decomposition

nodes.name: Rooted Degeneracy
nodes.statement: For $H$ and $U \subseteq V(H)$, the smallest $d$ such that there is an ordering $v_1,\ldots,v_{v(H)-|U|}$ of $V(H)\setminus U$ with $|N_H(v_i)\cap (U \cup \{v_j: j<i\})| \le d$ for all $i$.

nodes.name: Triangle Absorber Threshold
nodes.statement: $d_{\rm abs}(K_3) \le 3$.
conclusions: $d_{\rm abs}(K_3) \le 3$

nodes.name: $K_q$-Absorber Threshold for $q\ge 4$
nodes.statement: For $q \ge 4$, $d_{\rm abs}(K_q) \le q + 0.5$.
conclusions: $d_{\rm abs}(K_q) \le q + 0.5$

nodes.name: Yuster Random Fractional General
nodes.statement: Let $q \ge 3$, $a := \max\{d_{\rm abs}(K_q),(q+1)/2\}$. If $p \ge n^{-1/a+\beta}$, then a.a.s. $G(n,p)$ has a fractional $K_q$-decomposition.
conclusions: a.a.s. $G(n,p)$ has a fractional $K_q$-decomposition

nodes.name: Yuster Triangle Fractional
nodes.statement: If $p := n^{-1/3+\beta}$, then a.a.s. $G(n,p)$ has a fractional $K_3$-decomposition.
conclusions: a.a.s. $G(n,p)$ has a fractional $K_3$-decomposition

nodes.name: Yuster $K_q$ Fractional
nodes.statement: Let $q \ge 4$. If $p \ge n^{-1/(q+0.5)+\beta}$, then a.a.s. $G(n,p)$ has a fractional $K_q$-decomposition.
conclusions: a.a.s. $G(n,p)$ has a fractional $K_q$-decomposition

nodes.name: $K_q$-Omni-Absorber
nodes.statement: For a graph $X$, $A$ is a $K_q$-omni-absorber for $X$ with decomposition family $\mathcal{H}$ and decomposition function $\mathcal{Q}_A$ if $V(X)=V(A)$, $X,A$ are edge-disjoint, $\mathcal{H} \subseteq \binom{X\cup A}{K_q}$ with $|E(H)\cap E(X)|\le 1$, and for every $K_q$-divisible $L\subseteq X$, $\mathcal{Q}_A(L)\subseteq \mathcal{H}$ are pairwise edge-disjoint with $\bigcup \mathcal{Q}_A(L)=L\cup A$.

nodes.name: $C$-Refined Omni-Absorber
nodes.statement: A $K_q$-omni-absorber $A$ for $X$ with decomposition family $\mathcal{H}$ is $C$-refined if $|\{H \in \mathcal{H} : e \in E(H)\}| \le C$ for every edge $e \in X \cup A$.

nodes.name: Omni-Absorber Theorem (DPI)
nodes.statement: For each $q \ge 3$ there exists $C \ge 1$ such that: if $X \subseteq K_n$ with $\Delta(X) \le n/C$ and $\Delta := \max\{\Delta(X), \sqrt{n}\log n\}$, then there exists a $C$-refined $K_q$-omni-absorber $A \subseteq K_n$ for $X$ with $\Delta(A) \le C\Delta$.
conclusions: a $C$-refined $K_q$-omni-absorber $A$ exists with $\Delta(A) \le C\Delta$

nodes.name: Random Omni-Absorber Theorem
nodes.statement: For each $q\ge 3$ there exists $C\ge 1$ such that: with $a := \max\{d_{\rm abs}(K_q), (q+1)/2\}$, if $p \ge n^{-1/a+\beta}$ and $\Delta(X) \le pn/C$, then a.a.s. there exists a $C$-refined $K_q$-omni-absorber $A$ for $X$ with $A \subseteq (K_n\setminus X)_p$.
conclusions: a.a.s. a $C$-refined $K_q$-omni-absorber $A$ for $X$ exists with $A \subseteq (K_n \setminus X)_p$

nodes.name: Bipartite Hypergraph
nodes.statement: A hypergraph $\mathcal{G}=(A,B)$ is bipartite with parts $A,B$ if $V(\mathcal{G})=A\cup B$ and every edge contains exactly one vertex of $A$. A matching is $A$-perfect if every vertex of $A$ is in an edge of the matching.

nodes.name: Nibble with Reserves
nodes.statement: For $r\ge 2$ and $\beta\in(0,1)$, there exist $D_\beta, \alpha>0$ such that for $D\ge D_\beta$: an $r$-uniform multi-hypergraph $\mathcal{G}$ with $\Delta_2(\mathcal{G})\le D^{1-\beta}$ that is the disjoint union of $\mathcal{G}_1$ and a bipartite $\mathcal{G}_2=(A,B)$ satisfying degree conditions has an $A$-perfect matching.
conclusions: there exists an $A$-perfect matching of $\mathcal{G}$

nodes.name: Easy Perfect Matching
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal{G}=(A,B)$ is bipartite $r$-bounded multi-hypergraph and there exists $D \ge 1$ with $d_\mathcal{G}(a) \ge 8rD$ for $a\in A$ and $d_\mathcal{G}(b)\le D$ for $b\in B$, then $\mathcal{G}$ has an $A$-perfect matching.
conclusions: there exists an $A$-perfect matching of $\mathcal{G}$

nodes.name: Easy Perfect Matching Partition Version
nodes.statement: Generalization of Theorem 3.4 to a partition $A_1,\ldots,A_k$ of $A$ with separate degree thresholds $D_i$ on each part.
conclusions: there exists an $A$-perfect matching of $\mathcal{G}$

nodes.name: Proof of Easy Perfect Matching Partition Version
nodes.statement: Multiply edges to equalize $D_i$ across parts and apply Theorem 3.4.

nodes.name: Configuration Hypergraph
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{C}$ is a configuration hypergraph for $\mathcal{G}$ if $V(\mathcal{C})=E(\mathcal{G})$ and $E(\mathcal{C})$ is a set of matchings of $\mathcal{G}$ of size $\ge 2$. A matching of $\mathcal{G}$ is $\mathcal{C}$-avoiding if it spans no edge of $\mathcal{C}$.

nodes.name: $D$-Weighted Degree
nodes.statement: $w_D(\mathcal{H},v) := \sum_{i\ge 2} \frac{i-1}{D^{i-1}} \cdot |\{e \in \mathcal{H}(\{v\}) : |e|=i\}|$, and $w_D(\mathcal{H}) := \max_{v} w_D(\mathcal{H},v)$.

nodes.name: Bipartite Perfect Matching with Configuration
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal{G}=(A,B)$ bipartite $r$-bounded with $d_\mathcal{G}(a)\ge 300rD$ and $d_\mathcal{G}(b)\le D$, and $\mathcal{C}$ a configuration hypergraph with $w_D(\mathcal{C})\le 1$, then there is a $\mathcal{C}$-avoiding $A$-perfect matching.
conclusions: a $\mathcal{C}$-avoiding $A$-perfect matching exists

nodes.name: Random Sparsifications
nodes.statement: For $X$, $X_p$ is the random subset by independent inclusion with probability $p$. For graph $G$, $G_p$ keeps edges independently with probability $p$.

nodes.name: Weighted Hypergraph
nodes.statement: A weighted hypergraph is a pair $(\mathcal{F},w)$ where $w:E(\mathcal{F})\to \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$. Weighted degree $d_{\mathcal{F},w}(S) := \sum_{e\in \mathcal{F}(S)} w(e)$, and $\Delta_i(\mathcal{F},w) := \max_{|S|=i} d_{\mathcal{F},w}(S)$.

nodes.name: Kim-Vu Polynomial Concentration
nodes.statement: For all $k\ge 1$ there is $C\ge 1$ such that for $(\mathcal{F},w)$ $k$-uniform weighted hypergraph on at most $n$ vertices with $\mathcal{F}' := \mathcal{F}[V(\mathcal{F})_p]$: $\Pr[|w(\mathcal{F}') - \mathbb{E}[w(\mathcal{F}')]| > C\lambda^k\sqrt{E_0E_1}] < C\exp(-\lambda + (k-1)\log n)$.
conclusions: polynomial concentration bound on $w(\mathcal{F}')$ around its expectation

nodes.name: Kim-Vu Polynomial Form
nodes.statement: Under hypotheses with $\Delta_i(\mathcal{F},w) \le K p^i n^{-\beta}$ for all $i \in [k]$, with probability $\ge 1-n^{-\log n}$: $w(\mathcal{F}') = w(\mathcal{F})\cdot p^k(1 \pm n^{-\beta/3}\max\{\sqrt{K/w(\mathcal{F})},\, K/w(\mathcal{F})\})$.
conclusions: concentration of $w(\mathcal{F}')$ within polynomial factor of expectation w.h.p.

nodes.name: Proof of Kim-Vu Polynomial Form
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem 3.6 with $\lambda = 2\log^2 n$ and bound $E_0, E_1$ in terms of $K$.

nodes.name: Kim-Vu Multi-hypergraph Form
nodes.statement: For $k$-uniform multi-hypergraph $\mathcal{F}$ with $\Delta_i(\mathcal{F}) \le Kp^i/\log^{4k+2}n$, with probability $\ge 1-n^{-\log n}$: $e(\mathcal{F}') = e(\mathcal{F})\cdot p^k(1 \pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{\log n}}\max\{\sqrt{K/e(\mathcal{F})}, K/e(\mathcal{F})\})$, with corollary upper/lower bound forms.
conclusions: concentration of $e(\mathcal{F}')$ within logarithmic factor of expectation w.h.p.

nodes.name: Proof of Kim-Vu Multi-hypergraph Form
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem 3.6 with $\lambda = 2\log^2 n$ where $w(e)$ is multiplicity, then derive the upper/lower bound forms.

nodes.name: Embedding and $R$-Bridge
nodes.statement: An embedding $\phi: H\hookrightarrow G$ is an injective vertex map preserving adjacency. For independent $R\subseteq V(H)$, an $R$-bridge of $H$ is a component $J$ of $H\setminus R$ together with all edges from $V(J)$ to $R$. $\mathcal{B}(H,R)$ denotes the set of $R$-bridges.

nodes.name: Embedding Theorem
nodes.statement: For each $h\ge 1$ there exist $C\ge 1$ and $\varepsilon>0$ such that: if $H$ is connected, $R$ independent, every $R$-bridge has $\le h$ edges, every two vertices of $R$ in $\le h$ bridges, $\delta(G)\ge (1-\varepsilon)n$, and $p \ge n^{-1/m_2(S,V(S)\cap R)}\log^{8h+3}n$ for every $S\in \mathcal{B}(H,R)$ with $\Delta(H)\le pn/C$, then a.a.s. there exist $\psi$-respecting embeddings $\phi_S: S \hookrightarrow G_p$ with disjoint non-root pairs.
assumptions: every two vertices of $R$ in $\le h$ $R$-bridges
conclusions: a.a.s. there exist $\psi$-respecting embeddings of all $R$-bridges with disjoint non-root vertex pairs

nodes.name: Number of Embeddings Lemma
nodes.statement: For fixed $H$ and $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $\varepsilon'>0$ such that: if $\delta(G)\ge (1-\varepsilon')n$ and $p \ge n^{-1/m(H,R)}\log^{4e(H)+3}n$, with probability $\ge 1 - n^{-\log n}$ the number of $\psi$-restricted embeddings $\phi: H \hookrightarrow G_p$ is $(1\pm\varepsilon)\cdot n^{v(H)-|R|}\cdot p^{e(H)}$.
conclusions: $|\{\phi: H \hookrightarrow G_p,\, \phi|_R=\psi\}| = (1\pm\varepsilon) n^{v(H)-|R|} p^{e(H)}$ w.h.p.

nodes.name: Proof of Number of Embeddings Lemma
nodes.statement: Apply Corollary 3.8 (KimVu) to the multi-hypergraph $\mathcal{F}$ encoding $\psi$-respecting embeddings; bound codegrees via maximum rooted density and conclude concentration.

nodes.name: $B$-Degree Bound Lemma
nodes.statement: Under the embedding-theorem hypotheses, a.a.s. for every distinct $u,v\in V(G)$ and $m,b\in[h]$, the number of $R$-bridges $S$ with $e(S)=m$, $|V(S)\setminus R|=b$ and $\psi$-respecting embeddings using both $u,v$ outside roots is at most $n^b p^m / C'$.
conclusions: upper bound $n^b p^m / C'$ on number of $R$-bridge embeddings using a fixed pair $u,v$

nodes.name: Proof of $B$-Degree Bound Lemma
nodes.statement: Apply Corollary 3.8 to two auxiliary multi-hypergraphs $\mathcal{F}_{1,u,v}$ and $\mathcal{F}_{2,u,v}$ counting embeddings via $u,v$; use rooted $2$-density to bound codegrees and union bound over pairs.

nodes.name: Configuration Degree Bound Lemma
nodes.statement: Under the embedding theorem hypotheses with auxiliary hypergraph $\mathcal{H}$ on $R$, a.a.s. for every distinct $u_1,u_2\in V(G)$ and $m,b\in[h]$ the number of pairs of distinct $R$-bridges $S_1,S_2$ with roots in an edge of $\mathcal{H}$ and embeddings hitting $u_1,u_2$ is at most $n^{2b}p^{2m}/C'$.
assumptions: roots of every $R$-bridge in $\le h$ edges of $\mathcal{H}$
conclusions: upper bound $n^{2b}p^{2m}/C'$ on number of bridge-pair embeddings hitting $u_1,u_2$

nodes.name: Proof of Configuration Degree Bound Lemma
nodes.statement: Apply Corollary 3.8 to a multi-hypergraph $\mathcal{F}$ encoding pairs of edge-disjoint embeddings hitting $u_1,u_2$; partition by intersection of $\psi(V(S_i)\cap R)$ with $V(U_i)$ and use rooted $2$-density bounds.

nodes.name: Proof of Embedding Theorem
nodes.statement: Set up an auxiliary bipartite hypergraph encoding bridges and 2-element vertex sets, then apply Corollary 3.5 (and Theorem 3.7 for the moreover part).

nodes.name: Set up auxiliary bipartite hypergraph $\mathcal{G}=(A,B)$
nodes.statement: Let $A := \mathcal{B}(H,R)$ and $B := \binom{V(G)}{2}$, including for each $S\in A$ and $\psi$-respecting $\phi:S\hookrightarrow G_p$ an edge $\{S\}\cup \binom{\phi(V(S))}{2}\setminus \binom{\psi(V(S)\cap R)}{2}$.

nodes.name: Establish degree conditions a.a.s.
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 4.4, Lemma 4.5, Lemma 4.6 to obtain a.a.s. lower/upper bounds on $A$- and $B$-degrees and the configuration codegree bound.

nodes.name: Apply Corollary 3.5 for $A$-perfect matching
nodes.statement: By the partition $\{A_{m,b}\}$ and corresponding $D_{m,b}$, Corollary 3.5 yields an $A$-perfect matching of $\mathcal{G}$, giving the desired embeddings.

nodes.name: Bound $w_D(\mathcal{C})$ for the moreover part
nodes.statement: Construct a configuration hypergraph $\mathcal{C}$ with size-4 edges and bound $w_D(\mathcal{C})$ via the degree estimates; obtain $w_D(\mathcal{C}) \le 1$, then apply Theorem 3.7.

nodes.name: $2$-Density Concatenation Lemma
nodes.statement: For graph $H$ with independent $R\subseteq V(H)$ and proper induced subgraph $H_1 \supseteq R$ with $H_2 := H\setminus E(H_1)$: $m(H,R)\le \max\{m(H_1,R), m(H_2,V(H_1))\}$ and $m_2(H,R)\le \max\{m_2(H_1,R), m_2(H_2,V(H_1))\}$.

nodes.name: Proof of $2$-Density Concatenation Lemma
nodes.statement: Decompose $H_0\subseteq H$ as $H_0 \cap H_1$ and $H_0 \cap H_2$, and use convex combination on the densities; then case-analyse $v(H_1') \le 2$ vs $\ge 3$.

nodes.name: Anti-Edge and Fake Edge
nodes.statement: For $|S|=2$: ${\rm AntiEdge}_q(S)$ adds $q-2$ new vertices and edges $\binom{S\cup\{x_i\}}{2}\setminus\{S\}$. ${\rm FakeEdge}_q(S)$ adds $q-2$ new vertices and an anti-edge on each pair from $S\cup\{x_i\}$ except $S$.

nodes.name: Divisibility of Anti-Edge and Fake Edge
nodes.statement: If $F={\rm AntiEdge}_q(S)$, then $e(F)\equiv -1 \bmod \binom{q}{2}$ and $d_F(v)\equiv -1 \bmod (q-1)$ for $v\in S$, $\equiv 0$ otherwise. If $F={\rm FakeEdge}_q(S)$, then $e(F)\equiv +1\bmod \binom{q}{2}$ and $d_F(v)\equiv +1\bmod (q-1)$ for $v\in S$.
conclusions: divisibility properties of edge counts and degrees in anti-edge / fake edge gadgets

nodes.name: Density of Fake Edge and Anti-Edge
nodes.statement: For $q\ge 3$, $m_2({\rm FakeEdge}_q(S),S) = m_2({\rm AntiEdge}_q(S),S) = m({\rm FakeEdge}_q(S),S) = m({\rm AntiEdge}_q(S),S) = (q+1)/2$.
conclusions: all four density quantities equal $(q+1)/2$

nodes.name: Proof of Fake Edge / Anti-Edge Density
nodes.statement: Compute $m({\rm AntiEdge}_q(S),S)$ via $\binom{m+2}{2}-1$ formula, then bound $m_2$ via case split on $v(H'')$, and combine via Lemma 5.1.

nodes.name: Proof of Random Omni-Absorber Theorem
nodes.statement: Embed fake edges in slice $G_1\sim G(n,p_1)$ via Theorem 4.3 to refine the omni-absorber, then embed private absorbers in slice $G_2\sim G(n,p_2)$ via a second application of Theorem 4.3.

nodes.name: Choose constants and produce $A_0$ via Theorem 2.5
nodes.statement: Choose $C_1, C', C''$ from cited theorems, set $C := \max\{\ldots\}$, and apply Theorem 2.5 to obtain a $C'$-refined $K_q$-omni-absorber $A_0$ for $X$ in $K_n$.

nodes.name: Slice $G(n,p)$ into $G_1, G_2$
nodes.statement: Let $p_1 := \varepsilon p / (8C'')$ and $p_2 := p/4$, with $G_i \sim G(n,p_i)$ and $G'_i := G_i \setminus E(X)$ (and similar) so that $G_1 \cup G_2$ couples to $G(n,\le p/2)$.

nodes.name: Embed fake edges $H_e$ for each $e \in E(A_0)$ into $G'_1$
nodes.statement: For each $e \in E(A_0)$, let $H_e \cong {\rm FakeEdge}_q(e)$. Apply Theorem 4.3 with appropriate parameters to obtain $\psi$-respecting embeddings $\phi_e: H_e \hookrightarrow G'_1$ with disjoint non-root vertex pairs.

nodes.name: Construct $X'$ and refined decomposition family $\mathcal{H}_1$
nodes.statement: Let $X' := X \cup \bigcup_e \phi_e(H_e)$ and $\mathcal{H}_1 := \{(J\cap X) \cup \bigcup_{e\in J\setminus X}\phi_e(H_e) : J \in \mathcal{H}_0\}$, each element a $K_q$-divisible graph on $\le q^5$ vertices.

nodes.name: Embed private absorbers $A_J$ in $G'_2$
nodes.statement: For each $J\in \mathcal{H}_1$ select an absorber $A_J$ with $m_2(A_J,V(J)) \le d_{\rm abs}(K_q) + \beta/10$, then apply Theorem 4.3 with $H' := \bigcup_J A_J$ to embed all absorbers edge-disjointly in $G'_2$.

nodes.name: Assemble $A$ and verify omni-absorber properties
nodes.statement: Let $A := \bigcup_e \phi_e(H_e) \cup \bigcup_J \phi_J(A_J)$, with decomposition family $\mathcal{H}_A$ and decomposition function $\mathcal{Q}_A$ inherited from $A_0$ and the private absorbers; $A$ is a $C$-refined $K_q$-omni-absorber for $X$ in $G_1\cup G_2$.

nodes.name: $K_q$-Divisibility Fixer
nodes.statement: A graph $F$ is a $K_q$-divisibility fixer if for every $m\in \{0,\ldots,\binom{q}{2}-1\}$ and $(d_v\in \{0,\ldots,q-2\}: v\in V(F))$ with $\sum_v d_v \equiv 2m \bmod (q-1)$, there exists a spanning subgraph $F'\subseteq F$ with $e(F')\equiv m \bmod \binom{q}{2}$ and $d_{F'}(v)\equiv d_v \bmod (q-1)$.

nodes.name: Divisibility Fixer Fixes Divisibility
nodes.statement: If $G$ is a graph and $F$ is a spanning subgraph of $G$ that is also a $K_q$-divisibility fixer, then there exists $F' \subseteq F$ such that $G - E(F')$ is $K_q$-divisible.
assumptions: $F$ spanning subgraph of $G$ that is a $K_q$-divisibility fixer
conclusions: there exists $F'\subseteq F$ such that $G - E(F')$ is $K_q$-divisible

nodes.name: Proof of Divisibility Fixer Property
nodes.statement: Choose $m$ to make $m + e(G) - e(F)$ divisible by $\binom{q}{2}$, choose $d_v$ to make $d_v + d_{G-E(F)}(v)$ divisible by $q-1$, then apply the fixer definition.

nodes.name: Existence of Sparse Divisibility Fixer in $G(n,p)$
nodes.statement: For each $q\ge 3$ there exists $C\ge 1$ such that for all $\beta>0$: if $p\ge n^{-2/(q+1)+\beta}$, then a.a.s. $G(n,p)$ contains a $K_q$-divisibility fixer $F$ with $v(F)=n$ and $e(F)\le (q-2)n + C$.
conclusions: a.a.s. $G(n,p)$ contains a $K_q$-divisibility fixer $F$ with $\le (q-2)n + C$ edges

nodes.name: Strong $K_q$-Divisibility Fixer
nodes.statement: A multi-graph $F$ is a strong $K_q$-divisibility fixer if for every $m\in \{0,\ldots,q(q-1)-1\}$ and choice of $d_v$ with $\sum_v d_v \equiv 2m \bmod (q-1)$, there is $F'\subseteq F$ with $e(F')\equiv m \bmod q(q-1)$ and $d_{F'}(v)\equiv d_v \bmod (q-1)$.

nodes.name: Fat Triangle is Strong Fixer
nodes.statement: For each $q\ge 3$, a 3-vertex loopless multi-graph with $\ge q(q-1)$ parallel edges between every pair is a strong $K_q$-divisibility fixer.
assumptions: loopless 3-vertex multi-graph with $\ge q(q-1)$ parallel edges per pair
conclusions: it is a strong $K_q$-divisibility fixer

nodes.name: Proof of Fat Triangle Lemma
nodes.statement: Solve a 3-variable system of congruences $e_{xy}+e_{xz}\equiv d_x$, etc., choosing $e_{yz}, e_{xz}, e_{xy}$ in turn modulo $q(q-1)$.

nodes.name: Strong Fixer Inductive Step
nodes.statement: If multi-graph $F_1$ is a strong $K_q$-divisibility fixer and $F_2$ is obtained from $F_1$ by adding one vertex with $\ge q-2$ non-loop incident edges, then $F_2$ is also a strong $K_q$-divisibility fixer.
assumptions: $F_2 = F_1 + z$ with $\ge q-2$ non-loop edges at $z$
conclusions: $F_2$ is a strong $K_q$-divisibility fixer

nodes.name: Proof of Inductive Step
nodes.statement: Choose a set $X$ of $d_z$ edges incident to $z$, reduce to a fixer problem for $F_1$ with adjusted $d_v$ and $m$, then apply $F_1$'s fixer property and add back $z, X$.

nodes.name: Replacing Edge by Fake Edge Preserves Fixer
nodes.statement: If multi-graph $F_1$ is a $K_q$-divisibility fixer, $e\in E(F_1)$, and $X\cong {\rm FakeEdge}_q(e)$ is edge-disjoint from $F_1$ with $V(X)\subseteq V(F_1)$, then $F_2 := F_1 - e \cup X$ is also a $K_q$-divisibility fixer.
conclusions: $F_2 = F_1 - e \cup X$ is a $K_q$-divisibility fixer

nodes.name: Proof of Fake-Edge Replacement Lemma
nodes.statement: Use $F_1$'s fixer property to obtain $F'_1$; if $e\in F'_1$, replace it by $X$ and check the divisibility properties via Fact 5.3.

nodes.name: Proof of Sparse Divisibility Fixer in $G(n,p)$
nodes.statement: Build multi-graph $F_1$ (path power $P_n^{q-2}$ + fat triangle $S$), embed $F_1 - S$ via Park-Pham, then embed fake edges for $S$ in $G(n,p_2)$ via Theorem 4.3; apply Lemma 6.6 repeatedly.

nodes.name: Slice $G(n,p)$ into $G_1, G_2$
nodes.statement: Let $p_1 = p_2 = n^{-2/(q+1)+\beta}/2$ and $G_1\sim G(n,p_1)$, $G_2\sim G(n,p_2)$ coupled to $G(n,p_1+p_2-p_1p_2) \subseteq G(n,p)$.

nodes.name: Construct multi-graph $F_1$
nodes.statement: Form $F_1$ from $P_n^{q-2}$ by adding $q(q-1)$ parallel edges between vertices $v_1,\ldots,v_{\max\{3,q-2\}}$; show $F_1$ is a strong fixer by induction (Lemmas 6.4 and 6.5).

nodes.name: Embed $F_1 - S$ via Park-Pham
nodes.statement: Park-Pham yields a.a.s. $G(n,p_1)$ contains $(q-2)$nd power of a Hamilton cycle, so we may take $F_1 - S \subseteq G_1$ with bijection $\psi$ from $V(F_1)$ to $V(G_1)$.

nodes.name: Embed fake edges $H_e$ for $e \in S$ via Theorem 4.3
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem 4.3 (Embedding Theorem) to $H = \bigcup_{e\in S} H_e$ in $G_2 \setminus (E(F_1)\setminus S)$ to obtain $\psi$-respecting edge-disjoint embeddings.

nodes.name: Assemble $F$ via Lemma 6.6
nodes.statement: Let $F := (F_1 - S) \cup \bigcup_e \phi_e(H_e)$; apply Lemma 6.6 once per edge of $S$ to conclude $F$ is a $K_q$-divisibility fixer with $e(F) \le (q-2)n + C$.

nodes.name: Design Hypergraph
nodes.statement: ${\rm Design}(G,F)$ is the hypergraph with $V = E(G)$ and edges given by the subsets of $E(G)$ isomorphic to $F$.

nodes.name: Regular Cliques Theorem
nodes.statement: For each $q\ge 3$ there exists $C\ge 1$ such that for all $\beta>0$: if $p\ge n^{-2/(q+1)+\beta}$ and $S'\subseteq S\subseteq K_n$ with $\Delta(S)\le pn/C$, then a.a.s. there exists $\mathcal{D}\subseteq {\rm Design}((K_n\setminus S)_p\cup S', K_q)$ that is $((1/2)\pm n^{-\beta/8})\cdot p^{\binom{q}{2}-1}\cdot \binom{n}{q-2}$-regular.
conclusions: a.a.s. a regular sub-design hypergraph $\mathcal{D}$ of the appropriate degree exists

nodes.name: Edge-Gadget Proposition (GKLO)
nodes.statement: For $q>r\ge 1$, disjoint $|e|=r$, $|J|=q$, complete $r$-uniform $G$ on $e\cup J$: there exists $\psi:\binom{V(G)}{q}\to \mathbb{R}$ such that $\sum_{H\supseteq e'} \psi(H) = \mathbf{1}_{e=e'}$ and $|\psi(H)|\le 2^r r!$.
conclusions: existence of $\psi$ with the stated combinatorial-summation and bounded-magnitude properties

nodes.name: Fractional $K_q$-Decomposition
nodes.statement: A $K_q$-weighting is a function from $q$-cliques of $G$ to $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$. A fractional $K_q$-packing has $\psi(e)\in [0,1]$ for all edges, and a fractional $K_q$-decomposition has $\psi(e)=1$ for all edges.

nodes.name: General Boost Lemma
nodes.statement: For $q>r\ge 2$ there exists $\alpha>0$: given $r$-uniform $G$, families $\mathcal{H}, \mathcal{Q}$, $\phi: E(G)\to[0,1]$, $d>0$ satisfying the regularity condition, there is a $K^r_q$-weighting $\psi$ of $G$ with $\psi(e)=\phi(e)$, support in $\mathcal{H}$, and weights in $(1\pm 1/2)/d$.
conclusions: a $K^r_q$-weighting $\psi$ with $\psi(e)=\phi(e)$, support in $\mathcal{H}$, weights in $(1\pm 1/2)/d$ exists

nodes.name: Proof of General Boost Lemma
nodes.statement: Construct weights $c_e$ from $\phi$ and $|\mathcal{H}(e)|$, and weights $\psi(H) = 1/d + (1/d)\sum_e c_e \sum_{Q} \psi_{e,Q}(H)$ using Proposition 7.2; verify constraints.

nodes.name: Yuster Fractional Preliminary Lemma
nodes.statement: For each $q\ge 3$ there is $C\ge 1$ such that: if $S'\subseteq S\subseteq K_n$ with $\Delta(S)\le pn/C$, then there exists a fractional $K_q$-packing $\psi$ of $(K_n\setminus S)\cup S'$ with $\psi(e)=1$ on $S'$ and $\sum_{H\in\mathcal{H}(e)}\psi(H) + (1/p)\sum_{H\in\mathcal{H}'(e)}\psi(H)=1$ for $e\in K_n\setminus S$.
conclusions: a fractional $K_q$-packing $\psi$ with prescribed $S'$-weight and edge-degree property exists

nodes.name: Proof of Yuster Fractional Preliminary
nodes.statement: Construct $\psi_1$ on $\mathcal{H}'(e)$ uniformly, define $\phi(e) = 1 - \psi_1(e)/p$ and apply Lemma 7.5 (General Boost) to obtain $\psi_2$; let $\psi := \psi_1 + \psi_2$.

nodes.name: Yuster Fractional Concentration Lemma
nodes.statement: For each $q\ge 3$ there exists $C\ge 1$ such that for $p \ge n^{-2/(q+1)+\beta}$ and $\Delta(S)\le pn/C$: a.a.s. there exists a $K_q$-weighting $\psi$ of $(K_n\setminus S)_p \cup S'$ with weights in $(1\pm 1/2)/(p^{\binom{q}{2}-1}\binom{n}{q-2})$ and $\psi(e)=1\pm n^{-\beta/7}$ for all edges.
conclusions: a.a.s. there is a $K_q$-weighting on $(K_n\setminus S)_p\cup S'$ with concentrated edge weights

nodes.name: Proof of Yuster Fractional Concentration
nodes.statement: Define weighted hypergraphs $\mathcal{F}_{0,e}, \mathcal{F}_{1,e}, \mathcal{F}_{2,e}$ for $e\in S'$ and $e\in K_n\setminus S$; bound codegrees via rooted 2-density; apply Corollary 3.7 to control $\psi_p(e)$.

nodes.name: Define weighted hypergraphs and key quantities
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{H}_1, \mathcal{H}_2$ be cliques in $K_n\setminus S$ and those touching $S'$, with corresponding $\psi_1, \psi_2$ and weighted hypergraphs $\mathcal{F}_{0,e}, \mathcal{F}_{1,e}, \mathcal{F}_{2,e}$.

nodes.name: Bound weighted codegrees (Claims 7.10, 7.11, 7.12)
nodes.statement: Show $\Delta_i(\mathcal{F}_{j,e},w) \le K_{j,e}\cdot p^i\cdot n^{-\beta/2}$ for each weighted hypergraph using max-rooted-density bounds.

nodes.name: Apply Corollary 3.7 and union bound
nodes.statement: Apply Corollary 3.7 to obtain $\psi_p(e) = 1 \pm n^{-\beta/7}$ for each edge with probability $\ge 1 - n^{-\log n}$, then union bound.

nodes.name: Proof of Regular Cliques Theorem
nodes.statement: Sample each clique $Q$ independently with probability $\psi(Q)\cdot D/2$ from the weighting in Lemma 7.7; apply Chernoff and union bounds to show a.a.s. degree concentration.

nodes.name: Reserve Design Hypergraph
nodes.statement: ${\rm Reserve}_F(G,A,B)$ is the bipartite hypergraph $(A,B)$ with edges the subsets $S\subseteq A\cup B$ isomorphic to $F$ with $|S\cap A|=1$.

nodes.name: Random Reserve Lemma
nodes.statement: For $q\ge 3$ and $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $\varepsilon'>0$: if $\delta(G)\ge (1-\varepsilon')n$ and $p\ge n^{-2/(q+1)+\beta}$, then a.a.s. (1) every edge $e\in E(G)$ is in $(1\pm\varepsilon)\cdot p^{\binom{q}{2}-1}\binom{n}{q-2}$ $q$-cliques of $G_p+e$, and (2) every distinct $e,f$ are in at most $p^{\binom{q}{2}-1}\binom{n}{q-2}\cdot n^{-\beta/7}$ $q$-cliques of $G_p+e+f$.
conclusions: a.a.s. concentration of clique-degree for each edge and codegree bound for each pair

nodes.name: Proof of Random Reserve Lemma
nodes.statement: Apply Corollary 3.7 to weighted hypergraphs $\mathcal{F}_e$ and $\mathcal{F}_{e,f}$ encoding $K_q$-cliques containing $e$ (and $e,f$) to bound their weights, then take a union bound over all (pairs of) edges.

nodes.name: What Appears in $G(n,p)$ Lemma
nodes.statement: For each $q\ge 3$ there exist $C\ge 1$ and $\gamma>0$: with $a := \max\{d_{\rm abs}(K_q),(q+1)/2\}$, if $p\ge n^{-1/a+\beta}$ and $p\le p'\le (1+\gamma)p$ with coupling $G\subseteq G'$ a.a.s., then a.a.s. there exist $F, X, X', A\subseteq G$ and hypergraphs $\mathcal{G}_1, \mathcal{G}_2$ and $D, D'\ge n^{\beta}$ satisfying the divisibility-fixer, omni-absorber, regular-design, reserve, codegree, and reserve2 properties.
assumptions: coupling of $G\sim G(n,p)$ and $G'\sim G(n,p')$ with $G\subseteq G'$ a.a.s.
conclusions: a.a.s. existence of compatible $F, X, X', A, \mathcal{G}_1, \mathcal{G}_2, D, D'$ satisfying properties (1)-(6)

nodes.name: Proof of What Appears in $G(n,p)$ Lemma
nodes.statement: Slice $G(n,p)$ into 4 sub-graphs $G_1,G_2,G_3,G_4$ at densities $p_1,\ldots,p_4$; in each, apply Lemma 6.1, Lemma 8.1, Theorem 5.4, and Theorem 7.1 to obtain the divisibility fixer, the reserves, the omni-absorber and the regular cliques; finally verify the listed properties.

nodes.name: Choose constants and slicing densities
nodes.statement: Pick $C_1$ from Lemma 6.1, $\varepsilon_2$ from Lemma 8.1, $C_2$ from Theorem 7.1, $C_3$ from Theorem 5.4. Define $p_1 = p_2 = p/(16 C_2 C_3)$, $p_3 = p/(4C_2)$, $p_4$ chosen so that the slicing reconstructs $G(n,p)$.

nodes.name: Couple the slices and bound max degrees
nodes.statement: Couple $G'_i \sim G(n,p_i)$ with $G \sim G(n,p)$ so $G_i = G'_i \setminus \bigcup_{j<i} G_j$; by Chernoff $\Delta(G'_i) \le 2p_i n$ a.a.s.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 8.1 (Random Reserve)
nodes.statement: Apply Random Reserve Lemma to $K_n$ (and $K_n\setminus G_1$) to obtain a.a.s. clique-degree bounds (a)(b)(c)(d)(f) of the inner claim.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 6.1 to obtain divisibility fixer $F\subseteq G_1$
nodes.statement: By Lemma 6.1, a.a.s. $G_1\sim G(n,p_1)$ contains a $K_q$-divisibility fixer $F$ with $v(F)=n$ and $e(F)\le (q-2)n + C_1$.

nodes.name: Apply Theorem 5.4 to find omni-absorber $A\subseteq G_3$
nodes.statement: Since $\Delta(G_1\cup G_2)\le p_3 n/C_3$, by Theorem 5.4 a.a.s. there is a $C_3$-refined $K_q$-omni-absorber $A$ for $G_1\cup G_2$ with $A\subseteq G_3$.

nodes.name: Apply Theorem 7.1 to obtain regular design hypergraph $\mathcal{G}_1$
nodes.statement: With $S := G_1\cup G_2 \cup G_3$ and $S' := G_3\setminus A$, by Theorem 7.1 there is a regular subhypergraph $\mathcal{G}_1\subseteq {\rm Design}(G_3\cup G_4 \setminus A, K_q)$.

nodes.name: Define $X, X'$ and verify all six properties
nodes.statement: Set $X := G_2$, $X' := G_1\cup G_2$, $D, D'$ as in the proof, and verify (i)-(vi) using the Chernoff bounds and the inner claim.

nodes.name: Proof of Yuster Random General
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 9.1 with $G$ playing the role of both $G$ and $G'$; apply nibble with reserves (Theorem 3.3) to find a $K_q$-packing $\mathcal{Q}_1$ of $G\setminus(X'\cup A)\cup X$; use the divisibility fixer to find $F'$ so that $G\setminus F'$ is $K_q$-divisible; conclude $\mathcal{Q}_1\cup\mathcal{Q}_2$ is a $K_q$-packing with leave $\le e(F') \le (q-2)n + C$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 9.1 to obtain $F, X, X', A, \mathcal{G}_1, \mathcal{G}_2$
nodes.statement: By Lemma 9.1, a.a.s. there exist $F, X, X', A\subseteq G$ and hypergraphs $\mathcal{G}_1, \mathcal{G}_2$ and $D\ge n^\beta$ with the listed properties.

nodes.name: Apply Theorem 3.3 (nibble with reserves) for $\mathcal{Q}_1$
nodes.statement: From the regularity, reserve, and codegree properties, Theorem 3.3 yields a $(G\setminus(X'\cup A))$-perfect matching of $\mathcal{G}_1\cup\mathcal{G}_2$, equivalently a $K_q$-packing $\mathcal{Q}_1$ of $G\setminus(X'\cup A)\cup X$.

nodes.name: Use divisibility fixer $F$ to obtain $F'$
nodes.statement: By Proposition 6.2, choose $F'\subseteq F$ with $G\setminus F'$ $K_q$-divisible and $e(F')\le (q-2)n + C$.

nodes.name: Conclude using omni-absorber
nodes.statement: Let $L := X' \setminus (F' \cup Q_1)$ where $Q_1 := \bigcup \mathcal{Q}_1$; $L\subseteq X'$ is $K_q$-divisible, so by omni-absorber there is $\mathcal{Q}_2$ decomposing $L\cup A$; $\mathcal{Q}_1\cup\mathcal{Q}_2$ is the desired packing.

nodes.name: Sandwich Conjecture
nodes.statement: For $d\gg \log n$, there exist $p_*=(1-o(1))d/n$, $p^*=(1+o(1))d/n$ and a coupling $(G_*,G,G^*)$ such that $G_*\sim G(n,p_*)$, $G^*\sim G(n,p^*)$, $G\sim G_{n,d}$ and $\Pr[G_*\subseteq G\subseteq G^*]=1-o(1)$.
conclusions: existence of probabilities $p_*, p^*$ and coupling that sandwiches $G_{n,d}$ between $G(n,p_*)$ and $G(n,p^*)$

nodes.name: Sandwich Result (Gao-Isaev-McKay)
nodes.statement: The Sandwich Conjecture holds for all $d \gg \log^4 n / \log^3\log n$.
conclusions: Sandwich Conjecture holds

nodes.name: Proof of Yuster Random Regular General
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem 9.4 to sandwich $G_{n,d}$ between $G_*\sim G(n,p_*)$ and $G^*\sim G(n,p^*)$; apply Lemma 9.1 with $G_*, G^*$ playing roles of $G, G'$; nibble with reserves on $\mathcal{G}_1\cup\mathcal{G}_2$; use Theorem 3.4 with $\mathcal{G}'$ to cover $G\setminus G_*$; conclude via the omni-absorber.

nodes.name: Sandwich $G_{n,d}$ via Theorem 9.4
nodes.statement: By Theorem 9.4, there exist $p_*, p^*$ and a coupling such that a.a.s. $G_*\subseteq G\subseteq G^*$ with $G_*\sim G(n,p_*)$ and $G^*\sim G(n,p^*)$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 9.1 with $(G_*, G^*)$
nodes.statement: By Lemma 9.1, a.a.s. there exist $X, X', A\subseteq G_*$, hypergraphs $\mathcal{G}_1, \mathcal{G}_2, \mathcal{G}$, and $D, D'\ge n^\beta$ with the listed properties.

nodes.name: Apply Theorem 3.3 to obtain $\mathcal{Q}_1$
nodes.statement: Theorem 3.3 yields a $(G_*\setminus(X'\cup A))$-perfect matching of $\mathcal{G}_1\cup\mathcal{G}_2$, i.e. a $K_q$-packing $\mathcal{Q}_1$ of $G_*\setminus(X'\cup A)\cup X$.

nodes.name: Apply Theorem 3.4 (Easy Perfect Matching) to cover $G\setminus G_*$
nodes.statement: Restrict $\mathcal{G}$ to $\mathcal{G}'$; use the degree bounds to apply Theorem 3.4 and obtain $\mathcal{Q}_2$ covering $G\setminus G_*$ via the reserve $X'\setminus X$.

nodes.name: Conclude with omni-absorber decomposition
nodes.statement: Let $L := X' \setminus (Q_1 \cup Q_2)$; $L$ is $K_q$-divisible since $G$ is, so by the omni-absorber there is $\mathcal{Q}_3$ decomposing $L\cup A$; $\mathcal{Q}_1\cup\mathcal{Q}_2\cup\mathcal{Q}_3$ decomposes $G$.

nodes.name: Fractional $K^r_q$-Omni-Absorber
nodes.statement: $A$ is a fractional $K^r_q$-omni-absorber for $X$ with decomposition family $\mathcal{H}$ and decomposition function $\psi_A$ if $V(X)=V(A)$, $X,A$ edge-disjoint, $\mathcal{H}$ a family of $K^r_q$-subgraphs intersecting $X$ in $\le 1$ edge, and for every $\phi:X\to[0,1]$ there is $\psi_A(\phi):\mathcal{H}\to[0,1]$ with $\psi_A(\phi)(e)=\phi(e)$ on $X$ and $=1$ on $A$.

nodes.name: Omni-Absorber Implies Fractional Omni-Absorber
nodes.statement: Let $q\ge 3$ and $X$ a graph. If $A$ is a $K_q$-omni-absorber for $q(q-1)*X$, then $A$ is a fractional $K_q$-omni-absorber for $X$.
conclusions: $A$ is a fractional $K_q$-omni-absorber for $X$

nodes.name: Proof of Fractional Omni-Absorber Proposition
nodes.statement: Order edges of $X$ by $\phi$-value, define weights $w_i$ summing to $1$, and assemble $\psi_A(\phi)$ from the omni-absorber decompositions $\mathcal{H}_i$.

nodes.name: $K_q$-Transformer
nodes.statement: Let $L, L'$ be $K_q$-divisible graphs. A $K_q$-transformer $T$ from $L$ to $L'$ is a graph such that $V(L)\cup V(L')\subseteq V(T)$ is independent in $T$ and both $T\cup L$ and $T\cup L'$ admit $K_q$-decompositions.

nodes.name: Star Transformer for Triangles
nodes.statement: Let $q=3$, $L,L'\cong K_{1,q-1}$ with $L\cup L'\cong K_{2,q-1}$. For every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a $K_q$-transformer $T$ from $L$ to $L'$ with $m_2(T,V(L)\cup V(L'))\le q + \varepsilon$.
conclusions: a $K_q$-transformer $T$ from $L$ to $L'$ with $m_2(T,V(L)\cup V(L'))\le q + \varepsilon$ exists

nodes.name: Proof of Star Triangle Transformer
nodes.statement: Construct $T$ as a path $v_0\ldots v_{k+1}$ of length $k\ge 1/\varepsilon$ with internal vertices complete to $x, x'$; verify rooted density bounds.

nodes.name: Star Transformer General
nodes.statement: Let $q\ge 3$, $L,L' \cong K_{1,q-1}$ with $L\cup L'\cong K_{2,q-1}$. There exists a $K_q$-transformer $T$ from $L$ to $L'$ with $m_2(T,V(L)\cup V(L'))\le q+1/2$.
conclusions: a $K_q$-transformer $T$ from $L$ to $L'$ with $m_2(T,V(L)\cup V(L'))\le q+1/2$ exists

nodes.name: Proof of General Star Transformer
nodes.statement: Construct $T$ as a $(q-1)\times(q-1)$ grid with column cliques and (all but first row) row cliques, vertices not in first row complete to $x, x'$; bound max-rooted-density via direct counting.

nodes.name: Sparse Anti-Clique Absorber
nodes.statement: Let $q\ge 3$ and $L := \nabla_q\, K_q$. If $q=3$, then for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists a $K_q$-absorber $A$ for $L$ with $m_2(A,V(L))\le 3+\varepsilon$. If $q\ge 4$, there exists a $K_q$-absorber $A$ for $L$ with $m_2(A,V(L))\le q+1/2$.
conclusions: existence of a $K_q$-absorber $A$ for $L$ with the stated rooted-2-density bound

nodes.name: Proof of Sparse Anti-Clique Absorber
nodes.statement: Build $A := A_1\cup A_2\cup A_3\cup A_4$ via two iterated anti-edges, copies of $K_{q-2}$ joining edges of $S_2$ to $S'_2$, and copies of the star transformer $T$ rooted at suitable vertex sets; verify density via Lemma 5.1 and a series of claims.

nodes.name: Construct $A_1, A_2$ via iterated $\nabla_q$
nodes.statement: Set $S_1 := L = \nabla_q\, K_q$, $S_2 := \nabla_q\, S_1$, $A_1 := S_2$. Construct $A_2 := \bigcup_{i=0}^2 S'_i$ vertex-disjoint from $A_1$.

nodes.name: Construct $A_3$ from edge-bijection $\phi: S_2 \to S'_2$
nodes.statement: For each edge $e \in S_2$, add a new $K_{q-2}$-clique $Q_e$ complete to the ends of $e$ and $\phi(e)$; let $A_3$ collect these new edges.

nodes.name: Construct $A_4$ via star transformers
nodes.statement: Partition incident edges of each $v\in V(S_2)$ into sets $M_{v,j}$ of size $q-1$; for each $v, j, i$ attach a copy of the star transformer $T$ rooted at $\{q_{e,i}: e\in M_{v,j}\}\cup\{v,\phi(v)\}$.

nodes.name: Bound $m_2(A,V(L))$ via Lemma 5.1 and four claims
nodes.statement: Use Claims 10.4-10.8 (rooted-density bounds on $S'_0\cup S'_1$, $S_2\cup S'_2$, $A_3$, $A_4$, plus a discharging argument for $q=3$) and Lemma 5.1 to conclude $m_2(A,V(L)) \le q+1/2$ if $q\ge 4$ and $\le 3+\varepsilon$ if $q=3$.

nodes.name: $\nabla_q$ Construction
nodes.statement:
If $L$ is $K_q$-divisible, $A$ is a $K_q$-absorber for $L$, and $B$ is a $K_q$-absorber for $
abla_q\, K_q$, then $A' := 
abla_q\, L\cup
abla_q\, A\cup igcup_{Q\in \mathcal{Q}_1\cup\mathcal{Q}_2} B_Q$ is a $K_q$-absorber for $L$ with $m_2(A',V(L))\le \max\{(q+1)/2, m_2(B,V(
abla_q\, K_q))\}$.
conclusions: $A'$ defined above is a $K_q$-absorber for $L$ with the stated rooted-2-density bound

nodes.name: Proof of $\nabla_q$ Construction Lemma
nodes.statement: Construct two $K_q$-decompositions $\mathcal{Q}'_1, \mathcal{Q}'_2$ of $A'$ and $L\cup A'$ from the absorber decompositions of $A, L\cup A, B, B\cup\nabla_q K_q$; the density bound follows from Proposition 5.4 and Lemma 5.1.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorems 1.7 and 1.8 (Absorber Thresholds)
nodes.statement: Theorems 1.7 and 1.8 follow immediately from Lemma 10.4 (sparse anti-clique absorber) combined with Lemma 10.5 ($\nabla_q$ construction) and existence of $K_q$-absorbers.

nodes.name: Absorber Lower Bound Lemma
nodes.statement: Let $L$ be $K_q$-divisible and $A$ a $K_q$-absorber for $L$. If every vertex of $V(A)\setminus V(L)$ is incident with an edge of $A$ and there exist disjoint $K_q$-decompositions $\mathcal{B}_1$ of $A$ and $\mathcal{B}_2$ of $L\cup A$, then every vertex in $V(A)\setminus V(L)$ has degree at least $2q-2$ in $A$.
assumptions: every vertex of $V(A)\setminus V(L)$ in some edge of $A$
conclusions: every vertex of $V(A)\setminus V(L)$ has degree $\ge 2q-2$ in $A$

nodes.name: Proof of Absorber Lower Bound Lemma
nodes.statement: Use that incident edge $e\in A$ is in cliques $Q_1\in \mathcal{B}_1, Q_2\in \mathcal{B}_2$; their disjointness forces an edge $f$ at $v$ outside $Q_2$, giving another disjoint $(q-1)$-set of neighbors.

nodes.name: Lower Bound on $d_{\rm abs}(K_q)$
nodes.statement: For each integer $q\ge 3$, $d_{\rm abs}(K_q)\ge q-1$.
conclusions: $d_{\rm abs}(K_q) \ge q - 1$

nodes.name: Proof of Lower Bound Corollary
nodes.statement: Take $L$ $K_q$-divisible without $K_q$ subgraph; trim $A''$ to $A$ from $\mathcal{B}_2'\setminus \mathcal{B}_1'$ to ensure disjointness; then apply Lemma 11.1.

nodes.name: Value of $d_{\rm abs}(K_q)$
nodes.statement: For each integer $q\ge 3$, $d_{\rm abs}(K_q) = q$.

nodes.name: Optimal $K_q$-Leave Number
nodes.statement: For $q\ge 3$ and graph $G$, the optimal $K_q$-leave number is the smallest $k$ with $k\equiv e(G)\bmod \binom{q}{2}$ and $k\ge \frac{1}{2}\sum_{v\in V(G)} (d(v)\bmod (q-1))$. A $K_q$-packing $\mathcal{Q}$ is optimal if $e(G) - e(\bigcup \mathcal{Q})$ equals this number.

nodes.name: Optimal Leave Lower Bound
nodes.statement: For $q\ge 3$, if $\mathcal{Q}$ is a $K_q$-packing of $G$, then $e(G) - e(\bigcup \mathcal{Q})$ is at least the optimal $K_q$-leave number of $G$.
conclusions: $e(G) - e(\bigcup \mathcal{Q})$ is at least the optimal $K_q$-leave number

nodes.name: Proof of Optimal Leave Lower Bound
nodes.statement: Use that $e(\bigcup \mathcal{Q})\equiv 0 \bmod \binom{q}{2}$ and degree divisibility $d_Q(v)\equiv 0\bmod (q-1)$, then sum residues over vertices.

nodes.name: Optimal $K_3$ Leave for $G(n,p)$
nodes.statement: Open: can a.a.s. any individual instance of $G(n,p)$ in the relevant range have an optimal $K_3$-packing (leave $n/4 \pm O(\sqrt{n\log n})$)?

nodes.name: Perfect Matching of Odd-Degree Vertices
nodes.statement: If $p \ge n^{-1/2}$, then a.a.s. $G(n,p)$ contains a perfect matching of its odd-degree vertices.

nodes.name: Generalized Perfect Matching of Specified Parity
nodes.statement: Given $\phi:[n]\to \{0,1\}$ with $|\{i: \phi(i)=1\}|$ even, if $p\ge n^{-1/2}$, then a.a.s. $G(n,p)$ contains a perfect matching on $\{v_i: d_{G(n,p)}(v_i)\equiv \phi(i)-1 \bmod 2\}$.
